title: Proteomic characterization of sorted peroxisomes
projectDescription: Proteomic analysis of sorted peroxysomes (old, young, and middle-aged).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Peroxisomes isolation Peroxisomes were isolated using the Peroxisome Isolation Kit (Sigma-Aldrich, PEROX1). After centrifugation, cells were resuspended in Peroxisome Extraction Buffer (provided with the kit). Cells were homogenized using a 2ml Dounce homogenizer (Sigma-Aldrich, D8938) with Pestle B for 20-25 strokes.  Nuclei, big cellular fragments and intact cells were pelleted at 1000g and 2000g centrifugation for 10 minutes. The supernatant (cytosolic fraction) was then centrifuged again at 25000g for 15 minutes to pellet crucial peroxisome fraction (CPF). CPF pellets were resuspended in Optiprep Denstity Gradient Medium (supplied with the kit) to make final concentration of 22.5%.  Density gradient centrifugation was performing in 1.5ml ultracentrifuge tube with 20%-22.5% (CPF)-27.5% Optiprept for 1.5h at 100000g. After centrifuge, the top layers (20% and 22.5%) were aspirate off. The bottom layer which contained purified peroxisomes was kept on ice until FACS-sorting. Single-organelle FACS-sorting For separation of peroxisomal age-classes, peroxisome fractions were sorted on a BD FACSFusion sorter (lasers: violet 405nm, blue 488nm, yellow-green 561nm, red 633 nm) with a 70 µm nozzle (1.0 × ND filter). MitoTracker Green was detected in the FITC channel, and Snap-Cell 647-SiR was detected in the APC/A-647 channel, Snap-Cell TMRstar was detected in PE channel. Threshold were set with APC and PE channel at 500. FlowJo V10 analysis software (FlowJo LLC) was used for data analysis. All plots shown are dot plot. Peroxisomes and Mito-Pero were FACS-sorted and subsequently pelleted at 27000 g for 20 minutes. Supernatant was removed and pellets were lysed using RIPA buffer (with protease inhibitor and phosphatase inhibitor (Thermo) and then snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen and kept at -80 until Western blotting or MS analysis. Sample preparation for proteomic analyses Sorted cell pellets were re-suspended in RIPA buffer supplemented with protease and phosphatase inhibitors (Halt™ Protease Inhibitor and 0.5M EDTA; Thermo-Fisher), sonicated for 20min (20 cycles: 30s ON, 30s OFF; Bioruptor, Diagenode), and centrifuged at 14,000xg for 30min at 4ºC. Supernatants were collected. Protein concentration was measured by bicinchoninic acid assay (Thermo-Fisher) according to manufacturer’s instructions. Around 10µg of proteins were digested as in previously described protocols 1. Proteins were precipitated in methanol, incubated at -20ºC for 2h, centrifuged at 14,000xg for 20min at 4ºC, and supernatants were discarded. Protein pellets were re-suspended in 100mM Tris buffer containing 100mM dithiothreitol and 4% w/V sodium-dodecyl-sulphate (pH 8.0), heated at 95ºC for 30min under mild agitation, and diluted with 8M urea in 100 mM Tris buffer (pH 8.0). Samples were loaded on 30 KDa molecular filters (Millipore) and centrifuged at 14,000xg for 20min. Filters were washed twice with urea buffer, incubated in 50mM iodoacetamide in 8 M urea buffer for 30min (in the dark), and washed 4 times (2x 8M urea buffer, 2x 50mM tri-ethyl-ammonium bicarbonate buffer pH 8.0). Proteins were then digested using trypsin (enzyme-protein ratio 1:50) at 37ºC for 16h at 650RPM. After digestion, filters were centrifuged at 14,000xg for 20 min to extract tryptic peptides. Peptide mixtures were desalted and cleared of residual contaminants by sequential solid phase extraction. First, samples were loaded on primed (priming wash sequence: methanol, 80% acetonitrile (ACN) and 0.5% acetic acid in water, 0.5% acetic acid in water) C18 tips (Sigma), washed with 100µL of 0.5% acetic acid in ultrapure water, and eluted in 0.5% acetic acid and 80% ACN in ultrapure water. Eluates were dried in a vacuum concentrator. Second, eluates were dried and subjected to SP3 peptide purification 2. A volume of 2µL of SP3 beads (1:1 ratio of Sera Mag A and Sera Mag B re-suspended in ultrapure water; Sigma) was added to dried peptides and incubated for 2min under gentle agitation. A volume of 200µL of ACN was then added and samples were incubated for 10min. This step was repeated twice. Peptides were eluted from beads by adding 200µL of 2% dimethyl sulfoxide in water and sonicating mixtures for 1min. Supernatants were then collected, dried, and stored at -80ºC until MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass Spectrometry Analysis MS analysis was performed on a Q-Exactive HF-X (Thermo-Fisher) mass spectrometer. Around 1µg of tryptic peptides was separated on a RP-HPLC EasySpray column (ID 75 µm × 25 cm C18 2 µm 100 Å resin; Thermo-Fisher) coupled to a nano-LC EASY 1200 chromatography system (Thermo-Fisher). Peptides were first trapped on an Acclaim PepMap™ 100 pre-column (ID 75µm × 2cm C18 3µm, 100Å resin; Thermo-Fisher), then separated on a reverse phase HPLC EasySpray column (ID 75µm × 50cm C18 2µm, 100Å resin; Thermo-Fisher). Chromatographic gradient was run at a flow of 350nL/min with the following steps: 10-30% B in 90min; 30-45%B in 20min; 45-95% B in 1min; 95%B for 9.5min. Full MS scan parameters: 60,000 resolution, AGC target was set to 3E6. MS/MS scan parameters: 15,000 resolution, AGC target was set to 1E5. Collision energy was set to 28, n of analyzed peaks was set to 15. Dynamic exclusion window was set to 10s.  Mass spectrometry data processing MS analysis-derived RAW files were searched using the Andromeda 3 search engine as part of the MaxQuant 4 software suite (v1.6.14.0). Spectra were searched against the Uniprot-Swissprot human proteome database (version download: 2020.02.24). Trypsin was selected as protease for in silico digestion. Carbamidomethylation of Cysteine residues was selected as fixed modification, while Methionine oxidation and acetylation of N-terminal residues were selected as variable ones. Label-free Quantification (LFQ) 5 was activated to allow accurate evaluation of protein abundance. Identification of peptides resulting from missed cleavages was allowed. Precursor ion tolerance was set to 20 and 4.5 ppm for first and main searches, respectively. Match-between-runs option was enabled and settings left to default. The protein intensity table resulting from the search was filtered for protein q-value (< 0.01), contaminant (excluded), reverse sequences (excluded), and unique peptides (at least 1). Protein table was imported in R (v3.6), filtered for missing values (at least 75% observations in one sample group) and Log2 transformed. Residual missing observations were imputed with 0 prior centering and scaling the dataset.
